liaodactylus:eswiki:5.title: Liaodactylus (Cara lateral del cráneo y paladar)

facts.statement: Liaodactylus was described by Zhou et al. in 2017.
facts.quote: The genus contains one species, L. primus, described by Zhou et al. in 2017.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Liaodactylus is the holotype PMOL-AP00031, housed at the Palaeontological Museum of Liaoning.
facts.quote: There is one specimen of Liaodactylus known, namely the holotype PMOL-AP00031, which is stored at the Palaeontological Museum of Liaoning.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus lived during the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 161.8 to 159.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: These outcrops are considered to belong to the Late Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation, which has been dated to range from 161.8 ± 0.4 to 159.5 ± 0.6 million years ago (Oxfordian) based on argon-argon dating.

facts.statement: A 2023 study proposed that the Liaodactylus fossils belong to the Haifanggou Formation rather than the Tiaojishan Formation.
facts.quote: However, a 2023 study instead suggested that these deposits pertain to the Haifanggou Formation instead.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus was a filter-feeder equipped with approximately 150 long, comb-like teeth.
facts.quote: As an adaptation to filter-feeding, Liaodactylus had approximately 150 long, comb-like teeth packed closely together.

facts.statement: The jaws of Liaodactylus contained 152 long, needle-like, tightly packed teeth.
facts.quote: There are many long, needle-like, outward-projecting, tightly packed, equally-spaced teeth in the jaws of Liaodactylus, totalling to 152 teeth across both jaws.

facts.statement: The first tooth in each jaw of Liaodactylus was about half the length of the second tooth.
facts.quote: The first tooth at the front of each jaw is also somewhat shortened, being only half the length of the second.

facts.statement: When closed, the interlocking teeth of Liaodactylus formed a comb-like structure used for filter-feeding.
facts.quote: Collectively, the teeth, which would have interlocked when the jaw was closed, form a comb-like complex that would have been used for filter-feeding.

facts.statement: The jugal bone of Liaodactylus is bent slightly, creating a curved margin below the eye socket.
facts.quote: The bone is bent slightly such that the margin of the jaw below the eye socket is curved.

facts.statement: In Liaodactylus, the atlas and axis vertebrae are fused together, though a visible suture remains.
facts.quote: The atlas and axis are fused, albeit with a visible suture.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus is classified as a filter-feeding ctenochasmatid pterosaur from the Jurassic of China.
facts.quote: Liaodactylus is a genus of filter-feeding ctenochasmatid pterosaur from the Jurassic of China.

facts.statement: Zhou et al. assigned Liaodactylus to the family Ctenochasmatidae in 2017 using phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Zhou et al. assigned Liaodactylus to the Ctenochasmatidae in 2017 based on a phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Liaodactylus closest to Ctenochasma, sharing similar jaw-to-skull ratios and outward-angled teeth.
facts.quote: Within the Ctenochasmatidae, Liaodactylus was found to be closest to Ctenochasma, with which it shares the ratio of jaw-to-skull length and the teeth being angled out to the sides.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus was the first filter-feeding pterosaur found in the Yanliao Biota.
facts.quote: Liaodactylus represents the first Yanliao filter-feeding pterosaur.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus lived in a forested woodland environment containing conifers, cycads, and ferns.
facts.quote: In terms of environment, the Tiaojishan Formation represents a forested woodland with conifers, cycads, and ferns.

facts.statement: The climate where Liaodactylus lived was cool, temperate, wet, and seasonal, with a mean temperature below 15 °C.
facts.quote: Collectively, they indicate a cool, temperate, wet, and seasonal climate with a mean temperature below 15 °C.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus is classified within the family Ctenochasmatidae.
facts.quote: familia: Ctenochasmatidae

facts.statement: The genus Liaodactylus was described by Zhou et al. in 2017.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Zhou et al, 2017

facts.statement: Liaodactylus lived during the late Jurassic period, approximately 160 million years ago in the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 160 millones de años, en el Oxfordiense

facts.statement: As an adaptation for filter-feeding, Liaodactylus had approximately 150 teeth arranged very closely together like a comb.
facts.quote: Como adaptación a su alimentación por filtración, Liaodactylus tenía aproximadamente 150 dientes dispuestos muy juntos entre sí, como si fuera un peine.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus is the oldest known ctenochasmatid and the first known filter-feeding pterosaur from the Tiaojishan Formation.
facts.quote: EsI el ctenocasmátido más antiguo conocido y el primer pterosaurio filtrador conocido de la Formación Tiaojishan.

facts.statement: Only one specimen of Liaodactylus is known, the holotype PMOL-AP00031.
facts.quote: Solo se conoce un espécimen de Liaodactylus, el holotipo PMOL-AP00031

facts.statement: The Liaodactylus holotype was found in outcrops located about 500 meters west of Daxishan village in Jianchang, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Se encontró en afloramientos localizados a cerca de 500 metros al oeste de la villa de Daxishan, en Jianchang, Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The rock outcrops containing Liaodactylus date to the Late Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation, dated between 161.8 ± 0.4 and 159.5 ± 0.6 million years ago (Oxfordian).
facts.quote: Estos afloramientos son rocas que datan del Jurásico Superior en la Formación Tiaojishan, la cual ha sido datada en el rango de 161.8 ± 0.4 a 159.5 ± 0.6 millones de años (Oxfordiense)

facts.statement: The genus name Liaodactylus combines "Liao", a shortened form of Liaoning, with the Greek word dactylos meaning "finger".
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina el término Liao, un prefijo que es la forma acortada de "Liaoning", con el griego dactylos ("dedo")

facts.statement: The species name primus comes from Latin, referring to Liaodactylus being older than other ctenochasmatids.
facts.quote: el nombre de la especie, primus deriva del latín, en referencia a la mayor antigüedad de Liaodactylus en relación con otros ctenocasmátidos.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus had a large and slender head with a cranial length of 13.3 cm and a mandibular length of 11.7 cm.
facts.quote: La cabeza de Liaodactylus es larag y delgada, con una longitud craneana de 13.3 centímetros y una longitud mandibular de 11.7 centímetros.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus had approximately 152 needle-shaped teeth densely grouped and projecting outward in its jaws.
facts.quote: Hay varios dientes en las mandíbulas de Liaodactylus, los cuales tienen forma de aguja, se encuentran muy densamente agrupados (con espacios entre ellos similares) y se proyectan hacia afuera, totalizando unos 152 dientes en sus mandíbulas.

facts.statement: The teeth likely interlocked when the mouth closed to form a comb-like complex used for filter-feeding.
facts.quote: Los dientes, que pudieron haberse intercalado cuando se cerraba la boca, formaban colectivamente un complejo en forma de peine que pudo usarse para alimentarse por filtración.

facts.statement: Compared to other ctenochasmatids, the jugal bone of Liaodactylus was very narrow, especially below the eye orbit.
facts.quote: Comparado con otros ctenocasmátidos, el hueso yugal de Liaodactylus es muy estrecho, especialmente debajo de la órbita ocular.

facts.statement: The top of the braincase is formed by the fused frontal and parietal bones, which curve sharply downward at the back to give the skull a rounded appearance at the rear.
facts.quote: La parte superior del neurocráneo consiste de la fusión de los huesos frontal y el parietal, los cuales se curvan abruptamente hacia abajo cerca de la parte posterior y producen que el cráneo tenga un aspecto redondeado en su zona posterior.

facts.statement: At the back of the skull, the basisphenoid is short, wide, and plate-like, featuring a wide U-shaped notch at its front end.
facts.quote: En la parte posterior del cráneo, el basisfenoides es corto, ancho, y en forma de placa, y tiene una muesca ancha en forma de U en su extremo frontal.

facts.statement: The occipital condyle connecting to the vertebrae is spherical, causing the spinal cavity (foramen magnum) to be hidden when the vertebrae articulate.
facts.quote: En el basioccipital, el cóndilo occipital, el cual se conecta con las vértebras, es esférico; en consecuencia, la cavidad para la espina dorsal, el foramen magnum, queda oculto cuando las vértebras se articulan.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae atlas and axis are fused together, although a visible suture remains between them.
facts.quote: En cuanto a las vértebras cervicales, el atlas y el axis están fusionados, aunque con una sutura visible.

facts.statement: In front of the atlas lies a small, rudimentary proatlas that is symmetrical, plate-shaped, and has a projection at the front.
facts.quote: En frente del atlas hay un pequeño proatlas rudimentario, el cual es simétrico, en forma de placa, y tiene una proyección en el frente.

facts.statement: Zhou and colleagues assigned Liaodactylus to the family Ctenochasmatidae in 2017 based on a phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Zhou et al. asignaron a Liaodactylus a la familia Ctenochasmatidae en 2017 con base en un análisis filogenético.

facts.statement: Within the Ctenochasmatidae, Liaodactylus was found to be closely related to Ctenochasma, sharing skull-to-jaw proportions and teeth that point to the sides.
facts.quote: Dentro de los Ctenochasmatidae, se encontró que Liaodactylus era cercano a Ctenochasma, con el que comparte la proporción de la longitud de cráneo y mandíbula y que los dientes apuntan hacia los lados.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus lived during the Oxfordian stage, between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 154.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Liaodactylus is known from the Tiaojishan Formation, which along with the older Haifanggou Formation forms the Yanliao biota, a diverse and well-preserved association of Jurassic animals containing at least 40 species.
facts.quote: Liaodactylus es conocido de la Formación Tiaojishan, la cual junto con la más antigua Formación Haifanggou forman la biota de Yanliao, una diversa asociación de animales del Jurásico bien preservados que contienen al menos 40 especies.

facts.statement: The Tiaojishan Formation environment included forests with conifers, cycads, and ferns, such as Neocalamites, Coniopteris, Zamites, Czekanowskia, Sphenobaiera, Protaxodioxylon, and Xenoxylon.
facts.quote: En términos ambientales, la Formación Tiaojishan representa una zona de bosques con coníferas, cícadas y helechos. Las especies de plantas presentes incluyen a los cola de caballo Neocalamites carcinoides, N. narthosi y Equisetum sp.; los helechos árboreos Coniopteris hymenophyloides y C. margaretae; la cícada Zamites gigas; las enigmáticas gimnospermas Czekanowskia ketova, C. ridiga y Phoenicopsis speciosa; el gingko Sphenobaiera kazachstanica; el ciprés Protaxodioxylon jianchangense; y la conífera indeterminada Xenoxylon peidense.

facts.statement: Fossils from this area indicate a cold to temperate, humid, and seasonal climate with an average temperature below 15 °C.
facts.quote: Estos fósiles indican en conjunto un clima frío a templado, húmedo y un clima estacional con una temperatura media bajo los 15 °C.

facts.statement: Liaodactylus represents the first filter-feeding pterosaur found in the Yanliao biota.
facts.quote: Liaodactylus representa el primer pterosaurio filtrador de Yanliao.

rejected.statement: Liaodactylus is the earliest known ctenochasmatid and the first filter-feeding pterosaur found in the Jurassic Yanliao Biota.
rejected.quote: It is both the earliest known ctenochasmatid and the first filter-feeding pterosaur from the Jurassic Yanliao Biota.
